newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan hopes to set global standards in infotech.
newsitem.headline: Japan hopes to set global standards in infotech.

text.p: Japan is to launch a push next year for its next-generation information and communications technologies to become de facto international standards.

The Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications said on Wednesday it would choose about five multimedia projects to promote as global standards and give them subsidies of about 100 million yen ($793,000) a year for three years.

"It is too late to start selling finished products on the global market. We should propose our technology, rather than finished products, to international organisations in order to set de facto global standards," a ministry official said.
In the first year, the ministry plans to include among selected projects one on wide-band next-generation digital cellular phone technology, the official said.
The new subsidy programme will start in the year beginning on April 1, 1998.
Although Japan was one of the first countries to launch a mobile phone business, it has failed to make it a global format due to weak governmental backup, the official said.

Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp's mobile phone unit, NTT Mobile Communications, is planning experiments on the next-generation cellular phone technology involving Japanese, American and Swedish makers in a bid to make it a global format.
